notes: DISCOVERED during the advance-services-q3-2026-11-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). This calendar tracks no Quarterly Services Survey release at all — 28 advance editions and 28 full editions run on the same 2020-2026 grid and only the advance half was ever proposed. It earns a row for three reasons the proposer measured. (1) It is the SCORING DATE for the advance print's own claim: across 12 advance->full pairs harvested from Wayback captures of services/qss/qss-current.pdf (2019-09 -> 2026-03), the full report has revised the advance Selected Services Total headline q/q TEN times by nothing at all and TWICE by exactly 0.1pp (Q4 2023, 2.0% -> 1.9%, CB24-43; Q2 2024, 1.4% -> 1.5%, CB24-148) — median 0.00pp, max 0.10pp. The advance IS the number; this release is where that stops being an assumption. (2) It is the first full report on the AIES-restated basis Census names for the 2026-11-19 advance, which is the one condition that 0.10pp bound has never faced. (3) It is the release that PROVES the suspension rule: the Q3 2025 twin (CB25-162) published on schedule 2025-12-11 with $6,119.4B +2.4% (+/-0.4) after its own advance was suspended, and its Selected Services Total paragraph carries NO advance-revision sentence — the absence is the suspension's fingerprint in the primary text. Note the corridor asymmetry against the December cluster: this pair sits ENTIRELY inside the funded window, landing one day before cr-expiry-2026-12-11, unlike mtis-2026-12-16 which the sibling lane flagged as the cycle's genuine lapse-exposure test. Impact LOW and symbols empty: zero of 1,871 GDPNow vintages 2014-2026 name this survey, no house playbook is macro- or services-keyed. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
